question.leadin: This leader was assassinated by Nathuram Godse [God-say] in 1948.
question.text: Name this central figure of India's independence movement who was given the honorific "Mahatma," or "Great Soul."
question.clue: With Lord Irwin, this person ended the salt tax in exchange for ending the Salt March.

swap.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah is considered the father of this nation, which split from India in 1947. This nation still disputes the Kashmir province with India.
swap.clue: Following its independence, this country's southern border was demarcated by the Radcliffe Line.

question.text: A notable example of Mughul architecture is this white-domed mausoleum in Agra, built by Akbar's grandson Shah Jahan for his wife.
question.clue: This building's mausoleum has a reverberation time of 28 seconds, so that prayers conducted by the hafiz from the Quran would linger as long as possible.

swap.text: This emperor, the grandson of Akbar, was confined to Agra Fort by his son Aurangzeb when he fell ill in 1658. Name this ruler who constructed the Taj Mahal for his late wife Mumtaz Begam.
swap.clue: This ruler's daughter sent their favorite son's head to them in a box, and this ruler was placed under house arrest by their eventual successor following the Battle of Samugarh.

question.leadin: This country's fortress of Sigiriya was built by the king Kassapa.
question.text: Name this country that was home to the kingdoms of Polonnaruwa ("poh-luhn-uh-ROOV-uh") and Kandy. The Fourth Buddhist council was held in this country during the Anuradhapura ("uh-NOOR-uh-duh-POOR-uh") period.
question.answerHtml: Sri Lanka [or Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka]
question.clue: Failing irrigation tanks triggered the Great Famine in this country's Anuradhapura Kingdom, which fell to Chola invasions.

swap.leadin: This woman authorized a series of nuclear tests in Pokhran that were codenamed Smiling Buddha.
swap.text: Name this daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru, who was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards after ordering an attack that damaged the Golden Temple at Amritsar.
swap.clue: This leader ordered air strikes in response to Operation Chingiz Khan to support a "Liberation War" against a 1971 genocide launched by Operation Searchlight.

question.text: This man was a strong proponent of the partition. He served as leader of the Muslim League prior to the partition, and then as Pakistan's first governor-general afterward.
question.clue: This man declared a "Day of Deliverance" when, in protest of their country's entry into World War II, members of the Congress Party resigned from government.

swap.text: This Indian empire, ruled by kings such as Raja Raja and Rajendra, established control over much of maritime Southeast Asia in the early 11th century. It was part of a trio of kingdoms with the Chera and the Pandya.
swap.clue: The Maldives and the competing Pandya dynasty were conquered by Rajaraja I of this empire, who later built the Brihadisvara ] Temple.

question.leadin: It was founded in 1906, and called for a religious integrated, independent India until 1940.
question.text: Name this group which shifted positions in that year, working for the partitioned state that became Pakistan.
question.clue: Thousands of deaths followed this party's call for a general strike on Direct Action Day.

swap.text: The British moved from indirect to direct rule in this colony following the 1857 Sepoy Rebellion.
swap.clue: Lord Curzon established this colony's North-West Frontier Province, whose western border was set at the Durand Line to settle the Great Game with Russia.

question.leadin: Identify these events from the British colonization of India.
question.text: Cartridges of Enfield Rifles greased with pork fat incited this uprising in 1857, which began in Meerut after the Bahadur Shah was proclaimed emperor and was put down by Colin Campbell.
question.clue: This event saw the death of Henry Lawrence in the Siege of Lucknow.

swap.leadin: These writings were called "inscriptions of the dharma" by their creator.
swap.text: Name these writings, often inscribed on either pillars or rocks, and whose instances were accompanied by the planting of banyan trees and mango groves.
swap.clue: These documents outline a policy of proselytism towards the neighboring king Antiochus I, though they promote tolerance of all religions.

question.text: The Nizams once paid tribute to this empire that dominated the Deccan Plateau. Founded by Shivaji, it overtook the Mughals as a regional power and fought three wars with the British in the late 1700s.
question.clue: The position held by the Bhat family in this empire was that of Peshwa, and that held by Shuha and his grandfather was Chhatrapati.

swap.leadin: John Zephaniah Holwell wrote about a prison in this city, describing how 123 people died in one night due to heat exhaustion and cramped conditions.
swap.text: Name this city where Siraj ud-Daulah notoriously imprisoned British POW's.
swap.clue: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in this city with the support of Warren Hastings.

question.leadin: One of these objects named for the Allahabad Fort includes Late Brahmi inscriptions added by the Gupta, who built an "iron" one in Delhi.
question.text: Name this type of object which an earlier ruler topped with a statue of four lions and an abacus at Sarnath.
question.answerHtml: pillars [or columns; or pillar edicts; prompt on poles; prompt on edicts by asking “recorded on what objects?”]
question.clue: At Sarnath, a statue of four lions sat atop one of these non-rock objects which was used to display the edicts of Ashoka.

swap.text: Solomon and Sirimavo's daughter Chandrika Kumaratunga was nearly assassinated by this ethnic group's namesake "Tigers," an anti-Sinhalese militant group.
swap.answerHtml: Tamil [or Tamil Tigers; or Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam]
swap.clue: This ethnic group created "singing steps" leading up to one of their three "Great Living" temples; that temple depicted legends associated with 63 "poet-saints" of this ethnicity.

question.leadin: This sultanate was usurped by the Hindu banker Raja Ganesha, who made a deal with Muslim nobles that his son would convert to Islam and succeed him as Jalal al-Din.
question.text: Name this sultanate founded by Ilyas Shah, who moved the capital to Pandua and remained largely independent of Delhi. This late medieval sultanate expanded the trade of its lands' renowned muslin.

swap.leadin: They were named for named for a kingdom in southern India ruled by the Wodeyar dynasty.
swap.text: Name this series of four wars ending in 1799. At the end, the British defeated Hyder Ali and Tippu Sultan and annexed much of their land.
swap.clue: The second, which lasted from 1780-17884, was ended by the Treaty of Mangalore, and saw the defeat of Hyder Ali at Porto Nova and his subsequent death, leaving his kingdom to his son Tipu Sultan, who fought against Cornwallis.

question.leadin: This author of Secrets of the Bhagavad Gita worked to awaken political fervor through the newspapers Kesari and The Mahratta.
question.text: Name this founder of the Indian Home Rule League, a nationalist agitator who signed the Lucknow Pact along with Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
question.clue: During Curzon's rule, this polymath and president of the Indian Home Rule League proposed a campaign to boycott British goods and stop paying taxes after Curzon partitioned Bengal. This man signed the Lucknow Pact with Mohammad Ali Jinnah.

swap.leadin: One apocryphal account in this religion's history holds that the sixty-nine-year-old Baba Deep held his severed head on his body while storming a holy city in 1757.
swap.text: Name this religion whose members were massacred in the Chhota and Wadda Holocausts, which occurred in 1746 and 1762 at the hands of Lakhpat Rai and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
swap.clue: That monarch who followed this religion defeated the Afghan king Zaman Shah to capture Lahore, then declared himself a maharaja.
